title: Triage and Certification Ladder for New Models (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that formalizes a fast triage + multi-stage certification ladder for new model variants we consider for serving. The goal is to make intake repeatable, assign clear owners, and provide measurable gates so product/infra teams can decide whether a model can safely go into hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to: open-weight or externally hosted models proposed for Redwood serving (new checkpoints, major-variant tuning, or quantized builds).
- Excludes: internal tweak-only forks that do not change model spec (handled via light regression).

High-level flow (one-line):
  1) Intake triage -> 2) Smoke + quick prompts -> 3) Quantitative evals + signal checks -> 4) Certification ladder decision -> 5) Canary rollout + regression watch

Owners / RACI (first pass):
- Intake owner (first contact): Diego Martinez (solutions-eng)
- Applied ML lead (eval design): Aisha Patel
- Runtime compatibility & perf: Ben Cho (serving-runtime)
- Security & privacy review: Sara Liu (security-and-compliance)
- Release / rollout: Platform eng (rotating engineer on-call)

Phase 0 — Submission metadata (triage):
- Submitter must provide: model name & version, license, provenance (weights URL + checksum), expected tokenization, expected max sequence length, typical use cases, claimed FLOP/params, and a short note on upstream evals.
- Quick checks by intake owner (within 48h): license OK? size fits infra? tokenizer supported? obvs malware/backdoor red flags?
- Output: triage pass / hold. If hold -> list of blockers.

Phase 1 — Smoke & compatibility (48–72h):
Must be automated and runnable by infra devs. Quick checklist:
- Basic inference sanity: generate short prompts, confirm outputs not empty, no crash on streaming mode.
- Latency baseline: 8-token prompt, measure median p95 (single-request) on standard Dedicated instance (NVIDIA A100-ish equivalence). Record: cold start latency, warmed p50/p95.
- Memory/KV health: run up to typical max context window, verify no OOM or large memory spikes.
- Tokenizer alignment: tokenization of canonical prompts (english + ascii edgecases).
- Cost estimate: tokens/sec and estimated $/1M tokens (raw).
- Quick ownership decision: proceed to Phase 2 if smoke OK.

Phase 2 — Signal matrix & quantitative evals (1–2 weeks):
We evaluate model across a consolidated set of signals: quality, safety, robustness, calibration, and cost. Below are required datasets and target/pass thresholds (initial):
- Quality: task suites relevant to submitter use-case (e.g., summarization/qa/generation). Use our canonical probe sets. Pass if degradation <= 5% relative to baseline model on task-specific metric OR absolute metric >= baseline threshold.
- Hallucination / factuality: run 200-item probe set; target: hallucination rate < 8% for high-precision use cases, < 18% for exploratory.
- Toxicity & safety: automated classifiers + 500 seeded prompts; flagged rate must be below baseline; any high-severity failures require security sign-off.
- Calibration / confidence: probability or logit-based calibration checks on labeled sets; expected Brier/expected calibration error not worse than baseline by more than 10%.
- Robustness: paraphrase + typos probes: accuracy drop < 12% relative.
- Regression tests: run the current production regression suite (all active model routes) — zero critical regressions allowed; non-critical regressions require mitigations.
- Cost / throughput: sustained throughput targets depending on target environment: hosted (<X ms p95), dedicated (expected tokens/sec per GPU). Provide quantized profile if applicable.

Phase 3 — Certification ladder (decision matrix):
We propose a ladder with three outcomes: Green (certified), Amber (restricted), Red (reject). Decision combines signal matrix scores, risk profile, and business need.
- Green: meets all required pass thresholds; recommend immediate staged rollout.
- Amber: meets quality but has one or two non-critical regressions (e.g., minor accuracy dip on niche probes) or cost is high; can be deployed under restrictions (limited routes, canary percentage cap, or only as fallback). Requires a mitigation plan and weekly regression monitoring for first 4 weeks.
- Red: fails critical signals (safety, major regressions, OOM/persistent instability) — do not deploy. Provide remediation list.

Success criteria (example numeric summary):
- p95 latency (8-token warm) <= 450ms on standard spec for hosted candidates.
- Hallucination rate <= 8% (high-precision) or <= 18% (exploratory).
- Critical regressions = 0. Non-critical regressions < 2 per major route.
- Sustained throughput >= baseline_model_tokens_per_sec * 0.7 for dedicated deployment.
- Cost per 1M tokens <= 1.5x baseline OR clear ROI case documented.

Prompt suite & probe template (for reviewers to add probes):
- Each probe entry: id, intent, prompt text, expected behavior (pass/fail criteria), category (factuality / safety / tone / format), owner.
- Example probe:
  id: AM-P-001
  intent: Simple factual ask
  prompt: "Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?"
  expected: "Jane Austen" (exact or inclusion)
  category: factuality
  owner: Aisha Patel

Regression monitoring & alerts (post-certify):
- Deck: for first 30 days after rollout, run daily regression suite and surface: token-level cost, per-route latency, example drifted probes (top 10), and any new safety flags.
- Alert thresholds: >10% relative increase in p95 latency OR >2 newly failing probes => page on-call platform eng + applied-ml lead.

Rollout playbook (minimal):
- Canary 1: 1% traffic for 24h, run smoke/regression probes in production with sampling.
- Canary 2: 10% traffic for 48h, enable cost telemetry and compare to baseline.
- Gradual ramp to 100% with blackout windows and rollback hooks.

Owner checklist (ready-to-run):
- Submit PR with model profile JSON (weights, tokenizer, quantization notes).
- Attach results from automated smoke script (logs + perf numbers).
- Provide probe CSV (id, prompt, expected) and mapping to eval tasks.
- Security attestation from security-and-compliance (Sara Liu).
- Meet with platform eng to schedule canary window.

Open questions / TODOs (workout items):
- Define canonical baseline model per workload (we currently use multiple; pick a weighted baseline?).
- Finalize exact thresholds for hosted vs dedicated (need input from pricing/product).
- Add synthetic adversarial probe generation to catch subtle brittleness.
- Automation: tie the phase gates into CI so triage -> smoke -> phase2 runs can be triggered by PR.

Notes to self / pragmatics:
- Keep phase 1 scripts minimal; infra folks should be able to run them with a single command.
- For Amber outcomes, include a short public-facing note for CS to explain the limitation (so customers understand tradeoffs).
- We will iterate thresholds after onboarding 5–10 models. Establish a post-mortem cadence to adjust gates.

Appendix: quick commands (example):
- run_smoke.sh --model-checkpoint s3://... --out smoke-output.json
- eval-suite --profile am-probes.csv --model-checkpoint ... --report report.html

If you review: comment inline on the thresholds and add any probes you think should be required for your product area. This draft is intentionally conservative on safety, permissive on cost with negotiation.

---
Revision history:
- v0.1 (2024-01-10) initial drafter (Aisha)
- edits 2024-02-20: clarified canary windows and added owner checklist (Diego / Ben)

Unresolved: who signs final "green" certification for enterprise customers? (product + legal?)
